## Why This Is Asked
Evaluates plugin architecture, isolation, and runtime extensibility in CLI tooling.

## Key Concepts
- Command pattern in plugins
- Runtime registry with versioning
- Sandboxed loading and security
- Hot reload and fallback semantics

## Code Example
```javascript
export interface Command {
  name: string;
  description: string;
  execute(args: string[]): Promise<number>;
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you handle dependency conflicts and plugin sandboxing security concerns?
- What metrics would you collect to monitor plugin health and performance?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests runtime extensibility, registry design, non-blocking fan-out, and routing policy decisions. Also evaluates trade-offs between Strategy and Chain in a pluggable auditing pipeline.

## Key Concepts
- Runtime plugin registry and factories
- Non-blocking, bounded concurrency routing
- Per-event routing rules and backpressure handling
- Strategy vs Chain trade-offs in routing

## Code Example
```typescript
interface Event { source: string; severity: 'info'|'warning'|'error'; category: string; payload: any }
interface Auditor { log(event: Event): Promise<void> }
type AuditorFactory = () => Auditor
class AuditorRegistry { register(name: string, f: AuditorFactory); create(name: string): Auditor }
class Router { constructor(private reg: AuditorRegistry, private rules: Array<(e:Event)=>boolean>); route(e:Event): Promise<void> }
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test the registry and routing guarantees?
- What metrics would you collect for backpressure and throughput?

## Why This Is Asked
Shows how to design pluggable, runtime-extendable policy logic for high-stakes API gateways while avoiding restarts. Tests hot-swap safety and ordering guarantees.

## Key Concepts
- Strategy + Registry for dynamic rule loading
- Short-circuit evaluation and backpressure of policy decisions
- Atomic swaps for hot-reload without downtime

## Code Example
```javascript
interface Rule { apply(req: Request): { ok: boolean; reason?: string } }
class Registry { register(name: string, factory: ()=>Rule); create(name: string, ...args:any[]): Rule }
class PolicyPipeline { addRule(name: string, args?: any): void; evaluate(req: Request): { ok: boolean; reason?: string } }
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you handle rule dependencies and initialization order?
- How would you test hot-reload without affecting live traffic?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

Gateways must adapt routing logic without redeploys; runtime policies test flexibility and thread-safety.

## Key Concepts

- Strategy and Registry patterns
- Precedence and isolation
- Concurrency-safe dynamic registration

## Code Example

```javascript
interface Policy {
  matches(req: Request): boolean
  routeFor(req: Request): string
}
class PolicyRegistry {
  register(name: string, p: Policy, priority?: number): void
  resolve(req: Request): string | null
}
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How to handle conflicting matches and policy precedence?
- How would you hot-swap policies in a live gateway without dropping requests?
